title: Control Gap
summary: A control gap is the measurable difference between the protection an organisation believes it has and the protection that is actually implemented, operating and effective. Three distinct failure modes hide inside that single phrase, and separating them is the core skill. A design gap exists when no control addresses the risk at all, for example no privileged access review for a tier-zero identity store. An implementation gap exists when a control is defined but not deployed everywhere it is needed, such as endpoint detection present on workstations but absent on the servers that hold the crown jewels. An operating effectiveness gap exists when the control is deployed but does not function as intended, which covers disabled logging, alert rules that never fire, exceptions that quietly became permanent, and configuration drift after a change. Practitioners find gaps through several converging sources: control testing and walkthroughs, framework crosswalks against a target baseline, attack-path or red-team findings, audit and assessment reports, incident and near-miss analysis, and telemetry coverage checks that compare an asset inventory against the systems actually reporting logs. Ranking gaps requires more than counting, because a missing detection on an identity provider that can reach everything matters more than a missing hardening baseline on an isolated lab. Good gap registers record the evidence, the affected scope, the residual risk, the remediation owner, the acceptance criteria and the verification method that will prove closure, and they distinguish genuine remediation from documentation that merely restates the intent.
objectives: You will be able to separate design, implementation and operating effectiveness gaps when reviewing a control failure.
You will be able to build a telemetry coverage comparison between asset inventory and systems actually reporting logs.
You will be able to derive gaps from framework crosswalks, control testing and red-team findings rather than opinion.
You will be able to rank gaps by reachability and business impact instead of by raw count.
You will be able to write remediation entries with owners, acceptance criteria and a defined verification method.
You will be able to detect where a compensating control or accepted exception has become a permanent silent gap.

sources.label: NIST SP 800-53 security and privacy controls

beginner.definition: A control gap is the difference between the protection you think you have and the protection that truly works. The safeguard may be missing by design, deployed in only some places, or present but broken. Finding the real difference is what keeps a security plan honest.
beginner.whyItMatters: You can pass a checklist review while still being exposed. A gap hides in the space between the written policy and what runs on the machines. If nobody measures that space, you spend money on paper and get no real protection. Finding gaps early lets you fix the important ones before an attacker finds them for you.
howItWorks: List the risks you care about and the safeguards meant to reduce each one.
Check whether a safeguard exists at all, which is a design gap.
Check whether it runs everywhere it is needed, which is a coverage gap.
Test whether it truly works today, because that is an effectiveness gap.
Gather proof from control tests, audits, incidents and log coverage reports.
Rank the gaps by reach and business harm, then give each one an owner.
beginner.example: Imagine a building with a fire alarm policy on the wall. The policy says every floor has a smoke detector. On inspection, one floor has none, which is a design gap. Another floor has detectors that were never wired to the alarm panel, which is a coverage gap. A third floor has detectors with dead batteries, which is an effectiveness gap. Reading the policy alone told you nothing true.
takeaways: A written policy is not proof that a safeguard is installed or working.
Separate missing, partial and broken controls, because each needs a different fix.
Rank gaps by what an attacker could reach, not by how many you found.

exercises.title: Control Gap - EASY
exercises.summary: Recall and recognition: definitions, one clear answer, single-step questions.

exercises.title: Control Gap - MEDIUM
exercises.summary: Application: read a short log or alert and choose the correct next step.

exercises.title: Control Gap - HARD
exercises.summary: Analysis: a multi-step scenario with distractors, evidence to weigh, and a reason to give.

exercises.title: Control Gap - EXTREMELY HARD
exercises.summary: Synthesis under pressure: incomplete evidence, competing priorities, and a decision you must defend.
